summary: Giulia Porru worked in linguistics and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. under Giacomo Devoto at the University of Florence (circa 1933–1937), where she was appointed professore incaricato di filologia germanica in 1946.
Giuliana Martini is a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 2010, she held posts at both the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University.

Giuliana Stramiglioni specialized in Japanology, having studied under Giuseppe Tucci (circa 1932–1936). She taught Italian at the University of Tokyo (circa 1936–1965) and served as Professor of Japanese at Sapienza University of Rome (1965–1985).

Giuseppe Bardelli worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Giuseppe Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He held academic posts at the University of Pisa between 1843 and 1862 and taught Sanskrit at Florence (1859–1862).

Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti was a linguist who held professorships at the University of Bologna from 1797 to 1831, teaching Hebrew, Oriental languages, and Ancient Greek. He later became Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library in 1833.

Giuseppe De Lorenzo worked in Buddhist studies and geology. Educated at the University of Naples Federico II (circa 1890–1894) and a disciple of Karl Eugen Neumann, he served as Professor of Geology and Physical Geography at Naples (1905–1941).
Giuseppe Maria da Gargnano worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome and served as vice-prefect of the Tibet Mission in 1758.
Giuseppe Mezzofanti studied at the University of Bologna (circa 1793–1797) and later held a post there from circa 1803 to 1831.

Giuseppe Toscano specialized in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore (1938–1942) and served as Director of the Museo d'Arte Cinese ed Etnografico (circa 1965–1988).

Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and archaeology who earned his doctorate at Sapienza University of Rome. He taught in India, served as Professor at Sapienza (1932–1969), and founded the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giuseppe Turrini was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Padua and Pisa, training under Giuseppe Bardelli and Gaspare Gorresio. In 1860, he became Professor of Indo-European Philology at the University of Bologna.

Giuseppe Vignato works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at Peking University under teachers including Angela Falco Howard, Chongfeng Li, Su Bai, and Shichang Ma, and held an affiliation there attested in 2017.

Giuseppina Scalabrino Borsani was an Indology scholar who studied under Ambrogio Ballini at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore (circa 1929–1933). She later worked as an assistant there from 1954 to 1980.

Giyu Nishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Sylvain Lévi, and others. He was appointed an assistant at the University of Tokyo (1926) and professor at Toyo University (1927).

Glenn H. Mullin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche, and he founded the Mystical Arts of Tibet in 1984.
Glenn Wallis is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi and traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Glyn Richards specialized in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, studying at the University of Wales, Oxford, and McMaster University. He taught at Carleton University and spent 1973 to 1990 at the University of Stirling as Lecturer, Senior Lecturer, and Department Head.
Gnanawimala Chandima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Godabarish Mishra worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Ravenshaw College and the University of Calcutta. He served as a teacher at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya, headmaster at Chakradharpur High School, and Director at the University of Madras.

Godamune Chullanaga is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed degrees and diplomas at the Indian Cultural Centre, Sri Jinarathana Vocational Training Center, University of Kelaniya, and Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka.
